_doc: Phase 8.4 v1 — mock interview drill bank for /interview/ (src/mock-interview.js). keywords[] are lowercase tokens the heuristic self-check looks for in the candidate's answer (substring match); hint is a one-line model-answer cue shown in the debrief. No LLM — scoring is a transparent heuristic (answered + substance + keyword coverage).

questions.q: Tell me about yourself and why this role.
questions.hint: 60-second pitch: who you are, a proof point, why this role now.

questions.q: Describe a time you handled a production incident.
questions.hint: Use STAR: scope the impact, your actions, the fix, and the follow-up.

questions.q: Tell me about a disagreement with a teammate and how you resolved it.
questions.hint: Show you heard them, used evidence, and reached a shared outcome.

questions.q: Describe a project you're proud of and your specific contribution.
questions.hint: Emphasise what YOU did and the measurable result.

questions.q: How do you keep your skills current in a fast-moving field?
questions.hint: Concrete habits beat 'I read a lot' — name the labs, certs, sources.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you failed and what you learned.
questions.hint: Own it, show the lesson, prove the behaviour changed.

questions.q: Explain the shared responsibility model in the cloud.
questions.hint: Provider secures OF the cloud; you secure IN the cloud (data, IAM, config).

questions.q: When would you choose a managed database over self-hosting on a VM?
questions.hint: Managed trades control for less ops: patching, backups, HA out of the box.

questions.q: How do you design for high availability across availability zones?
questions.hint: Spread across AZs, load-balance, replicate data, automate failover.

questions.q: What's the difference between vertical and horizontal scaling?
questions.hint: Vertical = bigger box; horizontal = more boxes + a balancer (scale out).

questions.q: How would you control and reduce cloud spend?
questions.hint: Right-size, commit (reserved/savings), tag for visibility, set budgets/alerts.

questions.q: Explain how IAM least-privilege works and why it matters.
questions.hint: Grant only what's needed; roles over long-lived keys; shrink the blast radius.

questions.q: Walk me through a CI/CD pipeline from commit to production.
questions.hint: Commit → build → test → artifact → deploy to stages → monitor/rollback.

questions.q: What is Infrastructure as Code and why use it?
questions.hint: Declarative, versioned, reproducible infra you can review like code.

questions.q: How do you handle secrets in a deployment pipeline?
questions.hint: Use a secrets manager/Vault, inject at runtime, rotate, never commit them.

questions.q: Explain the difference between a container and a virtual machine.
questions.hint: Containers share the host kernel (lightweight); VMs virtualise hardware.

questions.q: What's a blue-green deployment and when would you use it?
questions.hint: Two environments, switch traffic for zero-downtime, instant rollback.

questions.q: A pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff. How do you debug it?
questions.hint: kubectl logs + describe; check events, probes, resources, config/secrets.

questions.q: Explain the CIA triad with an example of each.
questions.hint: Confidentiality (encryption), Integrity (hashing/signing), Availability (redundancy).

questions.q: You see a brute-force alert in the SIEM. Walk me through your triage.
questions.hint: Validate, scope source/target, contain (block/lock), escalate, document.

questions.q: What is the principle of least privilege and how do you apply it?
questions.hint: Grant minimal access, review regularly, prefer just-in-time elevation.

questions.q: Explain symmetric vs asymmetric encryption.
questions.hint: Symmetric = one shared key (fast); asymmetric = public/private pair (key exchange).

questions.q: How does multi-factor authentication reduce risk?
questions.hint: Adds a second factor so a stolen password alone isn't enough.

questions.q: What's the difference between IDS and IPS?
questions.hint: IDS detects and alerts; IPS sits inline and can block the traffic.

questions.q: Walk me through what happens when you type a URL and press enter.
questions.hint: DNS resolve → TCP handshake → TLS → HTTP request → response render.

questions.q: Explain the difference between a switch and a router.
questions.hint: Switch forwards by MAC (L2) within a LAN; router forwards by IP (L3) between networks.

questions.q: What is a VLAN and why use one?
questions.hint: Logical L2 segmentation: smaller broadcast domains, isolation, security.

questions.q: Explain how a TCP three-way handshake works.
questions.hint: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK establishes the connection and sequence numbers.

questions.q: What's the difference between TCP and UDP?
questions.hint: TCP is reliable/ordered with overhead; UDP is connectionless and fast.

questions.q: How does subnetting help in network design?
questions.hint: Splits a network into smaller segments — fewer wasted IPs, contained broadcast, cleaner routing.

questions.q: A server is running out of disk. How do you find what's using it?
questions.hint: df -h to spot the full mount, du to drill into the biggest dirs, check logs/inodes.

questions.q: Explain Linux file permissions (rwx) and how chmod works.
questions.hint: rwx for owner/group/other; chmod sets them numerically (e.g. 755) or symbolically.

questions.q: How do you investigate a process consuming high CPU?
questions.hint: top/ps to find the PID, inspect with strace, then renice or kill if needed.

questions.q: What is systemd and how do you manage a service with it?
questions.hint: systemctl start/enable/status <unit> manages services and boot persistence.

questions.q: How do you schedule a recurring task on Linux?
questions.hint: cron/crontab for classic scheduling, or a systemd timer unit.

questions.q: Explain the difference between a hard link and a symbolic link.
questions.hint: Hard link = another name for the same inode; symlink = a pointer to a path.
